# DPDP Act 2023 — Glossary

Alphabetically sorted terms with definitions and Act section references.

---

**Automated Decision** — A decision made solely by automated means, including profiling, without meaningful human intervention. *(Section 10, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Blocking of Access** — The power of the Central Government to direct any intermediary to block public access to information generated by a Data Fiduciary, in the interest of the general public. *(Sections 36–37, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Consent** — Free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous indication of a Data Principal's wishes, signifying agreement to the processing of their personal data for a specified purpose. *(Section 6, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Consent Manager** — A person registered with the Data Protection Board who acts as a single point of contact to enable Data Principals to give, manage, review, and withdraw consent. *(Section 2(7) and Section 7, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Cross-Border Transfer** — Transfer of personal data by a Data Fiduciary for processing to any territory outside India, subject to restrictions notified by the Central Government. *(Section 16, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Data Breach** — See *Personal Data Breach*.

**Data Fiduciary** — Any person who, alone or in conjunction with other persons, determines the purpose and means of processing personal data. *(Section 2(5), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Data Minimisation** — The principle that personal data collected must be limited to what is necessary for the specified purpose. *(Section 4(1), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Data Principal** — The individual to whom the personal data relates; in the case of a child, the parent or lawful guardian. *(Section 2(6), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Data Principal Duties** — Obligations imposed on Data Principals, including providing authentic information, not suppressing material information, not filing false or frivolous complaints, and complying with applicable laws when exercising rights. Breach may attract a penalty of up to ₹10,000. *(Section 15, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Data Processor** — Any person who processes personal data on behalf of a Data Fiduciary. *(Section 2(7), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Data Protection Board of India (DPBI)** — The adjudicatory body established under the Act to determine non-compliance, impose penalties, and direct remedial action. *(Sections 18–28, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)** — An assessment undertaken by a Significant Data Fiduciary to evaluate the impact of processing activities on Data Principals' rights. *(Section 10(2), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Data Protection Officer (DPO)** — An officer appointed by a Significant Data Fiduciary to serve as the point of contact for grievance redressal and compliance oversight. *(Section 10(2), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Digital Personal Data** — Personal data that is in digital form, or personal data collected in non-digital form and subsequently digitised. *(Section 2(8), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Erasure** — The deletion of personal data by the Data Fiduciary upon withdrawal of consent or when the specified purpose is fulfilled. *(Section 8(7), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Exemptions** — Certain processing activities exempted from DPDP Act provisions, including processing by State instrumentalities for national security, research and statistical purposes, and such other purposes as may be notified by the Central Government (e.g., startups). *(Section 17, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Grievance Redressal** — The mechanism by which a Data Principal may raise complaints regarding processing of their personal data, addressed by the Data Fiduciary or DPO. *(Section 13, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Key Managerial Person** — A senior officer (as defined under the Companies Act, 2013) designated by a Significant Data Fiduciary; the DPO must be appointed as a KMP. *(Section 10(2), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Lawful Purpose** — Any purpose that is not expressly forbidden by law. *(Section 4, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Legitimate Use** — Processing of personal data without consent that is permitted under specified grounds, such as voluntary provision, State functions, or employment purposes. *(Section 7, DPDP Act 2023)*

**MeITY** — Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, the nodal ministry responsible for administering the DPDP Act. *(Preamble, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Notice** — A communication given by the Data Fiduciary to the Data Principal describing the personal data sought, the purpose of processing, and the manner of exercising rights. *(Section 5, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Penalty** — A monetary penalty imposed by the DPBI for non-compliance, up to ₹250 crore depending on the nature and gravity of the breach. *(Section 33, Schedule, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Personal Data** — Any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data. *(Section 2(13), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Personal Data Breach** — Any unauthorised processing, accidental or unlawful disclosure, use, alteration, destruction, or loss of access to personal data that compromises its confidentiality, integrity, or availability. *(Section 2(14), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Processing** — Any operation or set of operations performed on digital personal data, including collection, storage, use, sharing, and erasure. *(Section 2(16), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Profiling** — Any form of automated processing to analyse or predict aspects of a Data Principal's behaviour, preferences, or interests. *(Section 10, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Purpose Limitation** — The principle that personal data shall be processed only for the specific purpose for which consent was given or legitimate use applies. *(Section 4, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Records of Processing Activities (RoPA)** — A documented record of all processing activities undertaken by a Data Fiduciary, maintained as evidence of compliance. The DPDP Act does not explicitly mandate RoPA; this is an inferred best practice from Section 8's general obligations. *(Section 8, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Retention** — The storage of personal data for the duration necessary to fulfil the specified purpose, after which it must be erased. *(Section 8(7), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Right to Correction** — The right of a Data Principal to have inaccurate or misleading personal data corrected or completed. *(Section 12, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Right to Erasure** — The right of a Data Principal to have their personal data erased when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is fulfilled. *(Section 12, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Right to Information** — The right of a Data Principal to obtain a summary of their personal data being processed and the processing activities. *(Section 11, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Right to Nominate** — The right of a Data Principal to nominate another individual to exercise their rights in the event of death or incapacity. *(Section 14, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Security Safeguards** — Reasonable security measures implemented by a Data Fiduciary to protect personal data, including encryption, access controls, and breach detection. *(Section 8(4), DPDP Act 2023)*

**Significant Data Fiduciary (SDF)** — A Data Fiduciary designated by the Central Government based on volume and sensitivity of data processed, risk to Data Principals, and other factors. *(Section 10, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Storage Limitation** — The principle that personal data shall not be retained beyond the period necessary for the specified purpose. *(Section 8(7), DPDP Act 2023)*

**TDSAT** — Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal, the appellate body for appeals against orders of the DPBI. *(Section 29, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Voluntary Undertaking** — An undertaking offered by a Data Fiduciary to the DPBI at any stage of proceedings, committing to specific actions or remediation. Acceptance is at the DPBI's discretion. *(Section 32, DPDP Act 2023)*

**Withdrawal of Consent** — The right of a Data Principal to withdraw consent at any time, with the ease of withdrawal being comparable to the ease of giving consent. *(Section 6(6), DPDP Act 2023)*
